correctness.rationale: For even q and q=5 the relevant groups have abelian nonidentity centralizers, making the noncentral commuting graph a disjoint union of cliques. For odd q>5, the involution class has n=q(q+chi)/2 vertices and regular degree (q-chi)/2, hence q(q^2-1)/8 edges; its clique number is at most 3 from the dihedral involution centralizer. Since every chordal graph with clique number at most 3 has at most 2n-3 edges and the involution graph has at least 2n edges, it is nonchordal. Chordality is hereditary under induced subgraphs.
